info.title: Rift Global Package API
info.description: REST contract for package capabilities, resolution, declaration search, and symbol reads.

post.description: Answers each canonical entry with a collected release of its package. An exact version answers with that release and a requirement with the newest release it admits; when the package holds no such release, the entry answers with the release nearest the version it names, for a requirement the lowest version it admits. An entry whose package holds no collected release answers as missing.

post.summary: Search package source for a pattern.
post.description: Returns the matches of one regular expression over the source files of selected exact package versions, in package order as the request lists them, then file path order, then match offset. The server verifies candidate files in that order and stops a page at `limit` hits, at `x-rift-page-files-max` files, or at `x-rift-page-text-bytes-max` bytes of verified text, whichever comes first; `next_cursor` continues where the page stopped, and a `result_truncated` warning names the bound.

post.summary: Find the declarations holding package positions.
post.description: Names, for each position in a file of an exact package version, the smallest declaration whose range holds it. A position in a type stub, such as a `.pyi` or `.d.ts` file, answers the declaration the stub describes: the module's declaration when the stub pairs with a module file. A position answers no declaration when the global index holds no release at that exact version, no file at that path, or no declaration holding the position. The server **MUST NOT** answer from another version, and **MUST NOT** move a position past its line or the text, or one inside a character, to a neighboring one.

PackageIdentity.description: One package as its package manager identifies it.

registry.description:
Canonical registry endpoint, including its path when that path identifies the registry.
Credentials, query and fragment are never part of this owner.

SourceUnitId.description: Physical source identity with a defining package or runtime owner, or a source resolver and canonical unit key. The codec validates decoded paths, UTF-8 and canonical percent-encoding before lookup.

SymbolId.description:
Identity of one symbol: the language, the path of the declaring file, and the provider's
stable qualified name for the declaration. No shipped provider puts the file path into a
qualified name, so a declaration moved to another file keeps its qualified name while its
identity names the new path. A `~N` suffix separates declarations the qualified name
alone cannot, such as overloads that dispatch separately.

Symbol.description:
Readable Symbol assembled from normalized Contributions. Source structure lives in Node
and is connected through Relationship.

container.description:
The symbol this one belongs to - the class that owns a method, the module that owns
a function. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method sits beside its type and a Rust
method inside an `impl` block, both naming the type here; absent at the top level.

document_local.description:
Whether language semantics confine this symbol to the document that declares it. The
provider classifies locality from its language model; absent when `false`.

documentation.description:
Doc comments attached to the declaration, with the markup format they were written
in. Absent when empty.

extensions.description:
Language-specific facts with no portable equivalent, namespaced by the provider that
emitted them. Absent when empty.

facets.description:
Portable classification for cross-language queries, absent when empty. The local
kinds `trait` and `interface` can both carry the `type` facet.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this Symbol across the whole workspace. Absent for an
unestablished symbol: no accepted evidence, or more than one, established its
identity.

kind.description:
What this symbol is in the provider's vocabulary, such as `trait`, `function`, or
`table`.

language.description: The language this symbol belongs to.

modifiers.description:
Language keywords qualifying the declaration: `export`, `async`, `const`. Absent
when empty.

name.description:
The human-readable name, as written in the source: `parseConfig`. Rendered
signatures live in `signatures`.

origin.description:
Where the declaration belongs and how it was produced. Absent when it says a
project declaration, authored, with no package - the common case.

signatures.description:
One entry per callable form, absent when empty. Where the language dispatches
overloads separately they are separate symbols joined by the `overloads` edge;
several entries here are alternative forms of one dispatch target, as
`typing.overload` writes them.

types.description:
The types this symbol carries, each tagged with the role it plays: a return type, a
field type, a bound. Absent when empty.

visibility.description:
How widely the symbol is visible, in the language's own terms - `public`, `private`,
`pub(crate)`. Absent where the language has no such concept.

SymbolOrigin.description:
Where a symbol belongs and how its declaration came to exist. Source location and
generation are separate: generated code can belong to the project or to a dependency.
Absent from `Symbol` entirely when it says a project declaration, authored, with no
package.

location.description:
Which of the four places the declaration belongs. Absent exactly when
`source_kind` is `synthetic`.

package.description:
The package that owns the declaration: present for `dependency`, and optionally
for `project`. Absent for `stdlib`, `external`, and a synthetic declaration.

runtime.description:
Exact runtime or compiler release that owns a standard-library declaration.
Mutually exclusive with `package`.

source_kind.description: Whether the declaration is authored, generated, or synthetic.

SourceKind.description: How source or a declaration came to exist.
x-enum-descriptions: A person wrote it.
A tool produced it from other source.
The provider minted it without any source text.

SourceLocationKind.description:
Which of the four places a declaration's source belongs, on `SymbolOrigin`. Package
ownership is the separate `package` field: a `project` declaration can carry one too,
and `dependency` always does.
x-enum-descriptions: Owned by the current workspace.

Owned by one resolved dependency. The ECMAScript built-ins, such as `Array`, belong
to the npm `typescript` package, whose `lib.*.d.ts` files declare them.

Installed with the language toolchain: `stdlib/rust`, `stdlib/node`, or
`stdlib/python`.
Outside the project, dependency graph, and standard library.

Language.description: A language name and its optional dialect, joined by `:`. `sql` and `sql:postgresql` are two languages with two symbol spaces.

Documentation.description: One block of documentation attached to a declaration, in the markup it was written in.

text.description: The body of the comment, with the comment syntax stripped.

DocumentationFormat.description:
Which markup the text is written in, since whoever displays a doc comment is the one that
renders it.
x-enum-descriptions: Plain text with no markup to render.
Markdown as authored in the source.

Extensions.description:
Facts a provider carries that the model has no field for, under a reverse-domain key.
Keys and values use RFC 8785 canonical JSON. Consumers skip entries they do not
implement.

ExtensionValue.description:
Versioned extension value. data is validated against the schema advertised for its key
and version.

data.description:
The value itself, shaped by whatever that key and version advertise. Rift carries it
and never interprets it.

version.description:
Which version of the key's advertised schema shaped `data`. A consumer skips a value
whose version it does not implement.

SymbolFacet.description:
One portable category a symbol falls into. Kinds are language-specific; facets are
shared, so a filter written once applies to every served language.
x-enum-descriptions: A named scope that groups declarations.
A compilation or import unit.
Names a type.
Holds a runtime value.
Can be invoked.
Belongs to a containing type.
Owns members of its own.
A declared input of a callable.
A generic parameter a declaration abstracts over.
Instances of it can be created.
Other types can inherit from it.
Other types can fulfil it.
Expands at compile time.
Exercises other code as a test.
Decorates other declarations.
Adds members to a type declared elsewhere.
One case of an enumeration.
A closed set of variants.
Another name for an existing symbol.
A member accessed like a field but backed by code.
Declared without a complete implementation.
Creates instances of its container.
Belongs to the type rather than an instance.
Its value can change after initialization.
Visible outside its declaring scope.
Marked as discouraged for new use.
Where execution starts.
Invoked through operator syntax.
Runs asynchronously.
Yields a sequence of values over time.

ExactKind.description: A provider-local kind preserving the construct name used by that language implementation.

Signature.description:
One callable form of a symbol: the text it renders as, the symbols that text points at,
and its structure. Overloads are separate entries.

display.description: The signature as a reader sees it, in the language's own syntax.

effects.description:
Effect keywords the declaration carries, in the language's own words: `async`,
`unsafe`, `pure`. The spelling is preserved and never mapped onto a portable
meaning; absent when empty.

extensions.description:
Signature facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted
them. Absent when empty.

language.description: The language whose syntax `display` is written in.

links.description:
Symbols named inside `display`, each with the byte range of `display` that names it,
so a renderer can turn the rendered text into links. Absent when empty.

parameters.description: Declared parameters, in source order. Absent when empty.

receiver.description:
The implicit first parameter - `self`, `this`. Absent for a free function, and for
languages that have no such thing.

returns.description:
What the call yields, absent when empty. An array because a language may return
several values, and because a declared and an inferred return are separate
bindings.

throws.description: Types this form declares it can raise. Absent when empty.

type_parameters.description:
The generic parameters this form declares, each as the symbol that declares it.
Absent when empty.

Parameter.description:
One parameter of a `Signature`: what it is called, the types bound to it, and how a call
may pass it. A receiver is one of these too, held in its own field because it has no
position in the parameter list.

default.description: The default value as written in the source. Absent where there is none.

extensions.description:
Parameter facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted
them. Absent when empty.

name.description:
What the parameter is called. Absent where the language allows an unnamed one, as
a positional parameter in a function type.

node.description: Where this parameter is written in the source.

optional.description: Whether a call may leave it out.

types.description:
What it accepts, absent when empty. An array because a declared type and an
inferred one are separate bindings.

variadic.description: Whether it absorbs the arguments that follow - `*args`, `...rest`.

NodeId.description:
Identity of one syntax-tree node. The byte range locates the node in the tree the request
targets; the fragment after `#` is its witness - the first eight lowercase hex characters
of the SHA-256 of the node's source bytes. The identity describes the node in the
revision the response names.

TypeBinding.description: One type a symbol carries, together with the role it plays for that symbol.

origin.description: Where the type fact came from.

role.description: The role this type plays for the symbol.

TypeBindingRole.description: What this type is to the symbol that carries it.
x-enum-descriptions: The type of the implicit first parameter.
The type a parameter accepts.
The type a call yields.
The type a field holds.
A constraint on a type parameter.
The type of a collection's entries.
The type a map is indexed by.
The type of the failure a fallible result carries.
The type an alias or wrapper stands for.
The type a generator produces per step.
The type awaiting the value resolves to.
The type that tags which variant a value holds.

TypeBindingOrigin.description:
Where the type fact came from. A declared type and an inferred one can both be present
and disagree, which is the interesting case.
x-enum-descriptions: Written in the source by the author.
Worked out by the provider from usage.
Required by the surrounding context.

TypeExpression.description:
How a type is written in the source, plus the symbol that declares it when one does. A
type with a declaration resolves to that symbol; a structural type - `string | null`,
`{ a: string }` - has the spelling and nothing to resolve to.

extensions.description:
Type facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the provider that emitted them.
Absent when empty.

language.description: The language the spelling is in, and so which provider produced it.

resolved.description:
The symbol that declares this type, where one does. Absent for a structural type,
which has a spelling and nothing to open.

source.description: The type as it is written: `Optional[Config]`, `&mut [u8]`, `string | null`.

SignatureLink.description:
One symbol named inside a rendered signature, with the byte range of that rendering which
names it.

range.description: Offsets into the rendered string in `Signature.display`.

symbol.description: The symbol that stretch of text names.

TextRange.description:
Half-open UTF-8 byte offsets over authoritative UTF-8 source. Every provider converts
from whatever its toolchain counts in at its own boundary, so two toolchains' column
numbers arrive here on the same scale. No JSON Schema keyword can tie one field to
another, so that `end` is never below `start` is asserted by the surface
validation tests instead.

end.description:
One past the last byte. Equal to `start` for an empty range, which is how a position
between two bytes is spelled.

start.description: First byte of the range, counted from the start of the file.

PackageContextEntry.description:
One package the workspace depends on, as its manifests and lockfiles state it.

Entries order by manager, then name, then the selector they state: a declared
requirement before an exact version.

availability.description: Whether a global package index can answer for this entry.

registry.description: Accepted registry endpoint. Absent for a path, Git repository or direct URL source.

requirement.description:
The version requirement a manifest declares. Absent when a lockfile pins the
version.

version.description: The exact version a lockfile pins. Absent when only a manifest names the package.

PackageAvailability.description:
Whether a global package index can answer for one package, and where the entry's
source comes from when none can.
x-enum-descriptions:
The entry names a package a public registry serves, crates.io, npm, or the
Python Package Index, or a standard library: `stdlib/rust`, `stdlib/node`, or
`stdlib/python`.

The entry names a path outside the workspace, or an archive at a path, that only
this machine can read.
The entry names a git repository.
The entry names a registry other than the public one its package manager reads.

The entry names a package fetched from a URL no registry serves, such as a uv
wheel URL or an npm tarball URL.
Accepted source evidence does not name the registry serving this entry.

PublicationFormat.description: Publication format used by the package index.

QueryTerm.description: One bounded member from the parsed query.

text.description: One parsed query term or phrase.

phrase.description: Whether the caller quoted this term.

prefix.description: Whether the remote index widens this term as a prefix.

Warning.description: One condition the caller must account for.

detail.description: Bounded explanation for the warning. The bound holds the longest `requirement_unsatisfied` detail the package fields admit: a 128-byte manager, and a 4,096-byte name, requirement, and version.

CapabilityBounds.description: Active server ceilings for requests and responses.

Capabilities.description: Capabilities and active bounds for the package API.

analyzer_revision.description: Analyzer revision used to produce declarations.

corpus_revision.description: Corpus revision used to answer reads.

documentation_revision.description: Documentation revision used for documentation reads.

PackageResolutionRequest.description: Canonical dependency context submitted for package resolution.

ResolvedRequirement.description: One submitted entry paired with the package that answers it: a requirement with the release it resolves to, or an exact version with the nearest collected release.

PackageResolutionResponse.description: Resolution result accounting for each submitted entry.

available_exact.description: Exact packages available in the global index.

resolved_requirements.description: Requirements resolved to exact packages, and exact versions the global index answers from the nearest collected release.

missing_exact.description: Exact packages absent from the global index.

missing_requirements.description: Requirements absent from the global index.

warnings.description: Conditions the caller must account for, absent when none applies. A `requirement_unsatisfied` warning names a requirement of `resolved_requirements` whose package lies outside the range the requirement states, since no collected release satisfies it; its `detail` reads `<manager>/<name> <requirement> answered by <version>`, as in `npm/typescript ~5.7.2 answered by 5.9.3`.

SearchScope.description: Package search reads public declarations from selected exact package versions.

packages.description: Selected exact package versions. Omitted or empty, use the newest collected stable version of each package, or its newest prerelease when no stable version is collected.

target.description: Which package results may be returned. Omitted, symbol.

IdentifierMatchClass.description: Match class established for one declaration identifier. A search hit that matches none of the requested identifiers reports `unknown`; a symbol lookup hit never does.

PackageSearchHit.description: One public package declaration returned by search.

line.description: One-based source line containing the declaration.

contributing_fields.description: Fields that contributed to ranking. `file_content` names a match inside the declaration, which the file's text holds.

PackageSearchPage.description: One ranked page of package declarations. A page **MUST NOT** take the response past `response_body_bytes_max`: the server stops it before the first item that would, and the page carries the items that fit, `next_cursor` at the first item left out, and a `result_truncated` warning.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page.

analyzer_revision.description: Analyzer revision used for this page.

corpus_revision.description: Corpus revision used for this page.

documentation_revision.description: Documentation revision used for this page.

PackageSymbol.description: One package declaration returned by symbol lookup.

line.description: One-based source line containing the declaration.

PackageSymbolPage.description: One page of package declarations. A page **MUST NOT** take the response past `response_body_bytes_max`: the server stops it before the first item that would, and the page carries the items that fit, `next_cursor` at the first item left out, and a `result_truncated` warning.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page.

analyzer_revision.description: Analyzer revision used for this page.

corpus_revision.description: Corpus revision used for this page.

documentation_revision.description: Documentation revision used for this page.

PackagePatternRequest.description: Regular expression search over the source of selected exact package versions.

pattern.description: Regular expression in the syntax of the Rust `regex` crate. The server matches it line by line: `^` and `$` match at line boundaries, and no character class matches a line feed. The inline flag `(?i)` makes it case-insensitive.

packages.description: Selected exact package versions. Omitted or empty, use the newest collected stable version of each package, or its newest prerelease when no stable version is collected.

PackagePatternDeclaration.description: The smallest declaration whose range holds a match. A match no declaration holds carries none.

line.description: One-based source line containing the declaration.

source.description: The declaration's source, when the request includes `source`.

PackagePatternHit.description: One match of the pattern in one package file.

line.description: One-based source line where the match begins.

size.description: Size in bytes of the file holding the match.

source.description: The line where the match begins, without its line ending, when the request includes `source`.

PackagePatternPage.description: One page of pattern matches. A page that stops before the last match carries `next_cursor` at the first match left out and a `result_truncated` warning naming the bound it stopped at. A page **MUST NOT** take the response past `response_body_bytes_max`: the server stops it before the first match that would.

items.description: Matches in package, file path, and offset order.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page.

analyzer_revision.description: Analyzer revision used for this page.

corpus_revision.description: Corpus revision used for this page.

PackageDeclarationRequest.description: Positions in files of exact package versions, each to name a declaration for.

position_encoding.description: How `character` counts within a line: UTF-8 bytes or UTF-16 code units, as the language engine that reported the positions negotiated.

positions.description: Positions to answer, each at most once.

PackagePosition.description: One position in one file of an exact package version.

path.description: Path of the file below the package root, using forward slashes, as in `src/lib.rs`.

character.description: Zero-based offset within the line, counted as `position_encoding` states.

PackageDeclarationResult.description: One submitted position and the declaration holding it, named by the identity package analysis mints in the position's package: `rift://symbol/<language>/<manager>/<name>@<version>/<path>/<qualified name>`.

kind.description: What the declaration is in the provider's vocabulary, such as `trait`, `function`, or `table`, as its `Symbol` carries it. Present exactly when `declaration` is.

PackageDeclarationResponse.description: One result per submitted position. A result without `declaration` names a position no declaration holds.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details for an application error.

RateLimitLimit.description: Bounded request limit for the current period.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Bounded requests remaining in the current period.

RateLimitReset.description: Unix seconds until the current rate limit resets.

Digest.description:
The first eight lowercase hex characters of a SHA-256, the same witness convention `NodeId`
uses. The full digest is computed and compared internally; only this short form ever
reaches the wire.

DocumentationBlock.description: Documentation metadata addressing bytes held by an existing content owner.

chunks.description: Existing ranked documents intersecting this block, in source order.

content_digest.description: Digest of the block's exact bytes.

heading_path.description: Headings owning the block, in increasing depth order.

identity.description: Digest of canonical source identity and structural position.

kind.description: Whether the range carries prose or code.

language.description: Authored code language, when supplied by the format.

line.description: One-based line where the block starts.

range.description: Exact range in the regular source or decoded notebook cell.

source.description: Source record containing revision, format, origin, and license facts.

symbol.description: Owning declaration for an attached comment.

DocumentationBlockKind.description: The content a documentation block addresses.
x-enum-descriptions: Authored prose and its markup.
Authored code without execution or inferred name resolution.

DocumentationChunk.description: A baseline search document intersecting one block.

identity.description: Existing symbol or text document identity.

range.description: Exact content range held by this document.

DocumentationContentIdentity.description: One content owner: a regular source or decoded notebook cell.

cell.description: Decoded cell when the parent source is a notebook.

source.description: Original workspace file or package source unit.

DocumentationContext.description: Bounded documentation context requested for one exact declaration.

documentation_revision.description: Documentation revision used for the reverse reference lookup.

references.description: References ordered by evidence, source, block range, and identity.

truncated.description: Whether the reference count or total excerpt bytes reached its bound.

warnings.description: Incomplete source conditions for requested excerpts.

DocumentationHeading.description: One heading in a block's ordered section path.

level.description: Heading depth established by the format parser.

name.description: Heading identity, including the parser's duplicate-heading disambiguator.

DocumentationHit.description: One documentation block projected from its existing content owner.

block.description: Exact block metadata, including source identity and range.

documentation_revision.description: Documentation revision under which this block was published.

source.description: Origin, revision, format, and license of the content owner.

DocumentationLicense.description: License metadata supplied by the source adapter.

expression.description: Declared expression; collection does not infer a license from source text.

files.description: License files whose bytes the adapter verified.

DocumentationLicenseFile.description: One license file's address and byte digest.

digest.description: Digest of the license file's original bytes.

path.description: Path relative to the source's project or package root.

DocumentationReference.description: An exact declaration reference authored inside standalone documentation.

identity.description: Digest of block, target, evidence, spelling, and occurrence ordinal.

range.description: Reference range in its content owner.

DocumentationReferenceEvidence.description: Evidence establishing a documentation reference, ordered strongest first.
x-enum-descriptions: A typed contribution naming an exact declaration.
An authored link resolving to one declaration location.
Inline code equal to one declaration's qualified name.
Inline code equal to one unique declaration name.

DocumentationReferenceHit.description: One exact declaration reference and the documentation containing it.

documentation.description: Source block and its origin facts.

excerpt.description: Bytes read from the existing content owner within the response bound.

reference.description: Exact reference evidence, never a repeated name lookup.

DocumentationSelectionReason.description: Why the caller selected this source.
x-enum-descriptions: Visible documentation in the captured workspace.
Source selected from one exact package's acquired bytes.
Comment supplied by its declaration's syntax provider.
Source supplied by a cloud resolver.

DocumentationSource.description: Source facts shared by every block belonging to one content owner.

byte_length.description: Exact content length in UTF-8 bytes.

content_digest.description: Digest of the content owner's exact bytes.

identity.description: Canonical address of the bytes block ranges use.

license.description: License facts recorded by the source adapter.

media_type.description: Media type supplied by the source adapter.

origin.description: Ownership and generation facts supplied by the caller.

physical_ranges.description: Original JSON string-token ranges for a decoded notebook cell, in source order.

revision.description: Source revision supplied by the caller.

selection.description: Why the source adapter selected these bytes.

x-enum-descriptions: Markdown block and inline syntax.
Recognized Markdown ranges inside MDX.
Supported reStructuredText block and reference syntax.
Plain text paragraphs.
Selected markdown and code cells from a notebook.
Documentation attached by a syntax provider.

oneOf.description: A visible workspace file.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace root.

oneOf.description: A source unit supplied by an exact package adapter.

DocumentationStage.description: The collection step reporting incomplete documentation.
x-enum-descriptions: Source selection and byte validation.
Format parsing and block extraction.
Authored link and declaration reference resolution.
Mapping metadata to existing ranked documents.

DocumentationWarning.description: One bounded warning with repeated conditions counted per source.

count.description: Number of items omitted or truncated for this condition.

kind.description: Typed condition the caller can inspect.

DocumentationWarningKind.description: Why one documentation source is incomplete.
x-enum-descriptions: Source bytes or their format are unavailable.
Retained source ends before an addressed range.

ProjectPath.description:
One path below the workspace root, using forward slashes and UTF-8 in Unicode NFC - Rift
normalizes what it emits and what it accepts, and compares byte-for-byte. The empty path
names the root itself. Absolute paths, backslashes, control characters, empty segments,
and `.` or `..` segments are refused before the filesystem is touched. The limit is 1000
UTF-8 bytes, not characters. A workspace holding two entries whose NFC forms are equal
fails the read that touches them with `content_unavailable`.

ReadWarning.description:
One warning attached to a read result. The answer stands; the warning carries evidence
of a condition the caller weighs before relying on it.

oneOf.description:
Framework context could not be resolved for one source. Ordinary syntax stands;
framework-specific facts whose context is missing are left out.

detail.description: The missing package version, configuration, or template source.

framework.description: The framework whose context could not be established.

unit.description: The source whose framework context is unresolved.

oneOf.description:
The lookup found no declaration under its name, language, and scope.
`alternatives` names up to three project declarations, ordered by the smallest
case-insensitive Unicode Levenshtein distance to their short or qualified names.
Equal distances use qualified name, then project path order. Revision reads
use that revision's declarations. A `global` lookup carries no alternatives;
an `all` lookup proposes project declarations alone. If complete closest ranking
exceeds `search.symbol_alternatives_work`, alternatives are empty and `detail`
carries the registered failure's message, recovery action, and observed work.

alternatives.description: Project declaration identities the caller can use to select another name.

detail.description:
Why closest declarations could not be selected within the work bound.
Absent when every selected declaration was compared or scope is `global`.

name.description: The declaration name the caller requested.

oneOf.description: Documentation collection or excerpt output omitted part of a selected source.

warning.description: Bounded source identity, stage, failure label, and omitted count.

oneOf.description:
The documentation this read projects onto crossed a bound, so no documentation
block joins the answer: declarations and files answer as they would without it.
The condition holds until the documentation it names changes.

detail.description:
Which documentation was left out and the bound it crossed - prose for a
reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The answer was computed from an index that lags the tree the read captured. Facts
derived from the index may miss the newest writes; the digests state which two
trees disagree. When the two digests are equal, the tree moved in recorded files
outside the syntax-indexed ones or in the configuration file, and `detail` says
which.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

index_tree_revision.description: Tree revision the published index covers.

oneOf.description:
The vector ranking holds no vectors for the tree this read captured, so the answer
was ranked lexically alone. The pass over that tree is still running, or the tree
was published after the corpus the ranking holds was described. `prepared` and
`total` state how far the ranking has got for the captured tree, and `ready_in` is
derived from workspace size and embedding progress.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

prepared.description: Declarations of the captured tree that already carry a vector.

ready_in.description:
Estimated wait before the vector ranking joins an answer, not a measurement
of this machine. A caller may report it and must not schedule against it.

total.description: Declarations the set being embedded holds.

oneOf.description:
The local index is still preparing selected workspace files. The answer covers only
files whose capture and analysis have finished; `total` is absent until discovery ends.

detail.description: Why the local index is preparing - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

prepared.description: Selected workspace files whose capture and analysis have finished.

ready_in.description: Estimated wait before local preparation finishes. No estimate is available yet.

total.description: Selected workspace files, once discovery has finished.

oneOf.description:
The vector ranking will not answer for the life of this server, so every answer
is ranked lexically alone. No retry is coming: fix the `[search.vector]`
configuration and start the server again.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The full-text tier did not rank this answer, so it came from identifier matching
alone: a query phrased as prose finds nothing. The tier is still committing the
captured tree, missed a commit, holds no indexed tree, failed to load, got no
database connection within `[search] busy_timeout`, or still answers for a newer
publication after the request's capture attempts; `detail` names which, and what
clears it.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The query carried more terms and quoted phrases than `terms_max`, so the server
dropped the shortest unquoted terms and ranked the answer by the rest. Every
quoted phrase is kept. Shorten `query`, or quote the terms that must be matched.

terms_max.description:
Terms and quoted phrases the query was cut to: the server's bound on one
parsed query.

oneOf.description:
The lexical ranking stopped at `matches_max` units; hits past it never reached the
page, whatever `paths` selects. Narrow `query`.

matches_max.description: Units the ranking stopped at: the server's bound on one lexical ranking.

oneOf.description:
The server reached `results_max`, its result bound, before ordering and paging:
what the bound cut never reaches any page, and `total_pages` counts only what fit.
The bound cuts the ranked candidates and the hit set alike. The warning means the
bound was reached; a set of exactly `results_max` hits carries it too. Narrow
`query` or `paths`.

results_max.description:
The bound the read stopped at: the server's limit on both the candidates one
read ranks and the hits it returns.

oneOf.description:
A file held more matches of `pattern` than `matches_per_file`, so its later matches
are missing from this answer while every other file answers in full. `files` names
the cut files in project-path order, at most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of them. Narrow
`pattern` or `paths`, or raise the `[search]` key `pattern_matches_per_file`.

files.description: The files cut at the bound.

matches_per_file.description: Matches one file contributes at most: the server's bound on one file's matches.

oneOf.description:
The trigram index `pattern` selects its files through lacks rows of stored file
text, and verifying those rows beside the selected ones would pass the `[search]`
key `pattern_candidate_rows` or `pattern_verified_size`, so the answer covers the
rows the index holds and a match in the other rows is missing from it. The server
indexes those rows in the background after each write; `prepared` and `total` state
how far it has got. Resend the request once the index has caught up.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

prepared.description:
Rows of stored file text the trigram index holds: one per file, or one per
chunk of a file split under `[search.text]`.

total.description: Rows of stored file text the store holds.

oneOf.description:
A file answers nothing from its bytes. Either the index left the claimed file out -
its bytes are not valid UTF-8, or it crosses a per-file bound - so it answers no
search or lookup, and addressing it directly still refuses `content_unavailable`;
or a comparison against the working tree read the changed file in no working form -
its attributes name a `filter` driver or a UTF-16 `working-tree-encoding` - so it
answers changed with no declarations. Every other file in the workspace stays
available. At most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of this warning name a file, in
project-path order; when more files are named, one more carries no `unit` and
counts the rest. `rift server logs` names each file the index left out, and `paths`
narrows a comparison onto the others.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

unit.description:
The file the warning names. Absent on the one warning that counts the files
past `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX`.

oneOf.description:
Text files past `[search.text] max_chunk` are left out of the text index under the
key `large_files = "skip"`, so no hit answers from their text; `skipped` counts the
ones the request's `paths` reach. A declaration such a file holds still answers.
Setting `large_files` to `split` indexes them in chunks.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

skipped.description: The files past `max_chunk` the request's `paths` reach.

oneOf.description:
Files past `[providers.syntax] max_file` are held as text the syntax provider does
not parse: their text answers `search`, and none of their declarations were
extracted, so no symbol hit and no `get_symbol` answer comes from them. `files`
names them in project-path order, at most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of them. Raising
`max_file` parses them.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

files.description: The files held as text alone.

oneOf.description:
A lockfile the request's `paths.include` selects is left out of search, so no hit
answers from it; `rift://map` still carries the versions it pins. Naming the file
in `paths.force_include` searches it for one request, and removing its name from
the `[search.text]` key `excluded_lockfiles` indexes it. One warning names every
such file, in project-path order, at most `SOURCE_WARNINGS_MAX` of them.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

files.description: The selected lockfiles search leaves out.

oneOf.description:
Contributions selected for one symbol's presentation disagree on at least one
field. The answer carries what normalization selected.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

providers.description:
Providers whose Contribution carries a differing value for at least one
presentation field, sorted and deduplicated.

symbol.description: The symbol whose presentation facts disagree.

oneOf.description:
A traversal walk stopped at its node bound before exhausting the reachable graph,
so hits reachable beyond the bound are missing from this answer. Narrow the walk -
a tighter `facets` list, a smaller `depth`, or a less-connected seed - to fit it
under the bound.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

visited.description: Symbols the walk visited before it stopped, equal to the bound it hit.

oneOf.description:
No lane populates part of the relationship coverage the traversal asked for, so the
walk had nothing to follow there whatever the graph holds. The warning states that a
lane is absent; it never states that the seed has no such neighbor. An empty answer
carrying it means the walk could not run; an empty answer without it means the walk
ran and the seed has no neighbor under the request.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

facets.description:
The requested facets no lane populates, in the request's own order,
deduplicated. Absent when every requested facet has a lane.

oneOf.description:
A language engine serves the seed's language, and this read carries none of its
edges: the engine answered about bytes the served revision does not carry, answered
more than the walk's node bound holds, or was still analyzing when
`[server] readiness_timeout` was spent. The indexed relationships stand; whatever
the engine resolves on top of them is missing. The warning states that an engine's
analysis is absent from this answer; it never states that the seed has no such
neighbor. An engine still analyzing keeps loading, and a later read, served from a
revision the engine has caught up with or sent once it reads ready, carries the
engine's edges again.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

language.description: The seed declaration's language, whose engine's answer was dropped.

oneOf.description:
An outgoing walk dropped its edges to callees it named no declaration for. The
language engine's call hierarchy named each in a file outside the project and every
installed package the workspace's dependencies name, or in a package or standard
library file where the global index answered no declaration at the callee's
position. Every package callee drops when the global API is off or did not answer,
and the answer then carries the global warning naming why. Every other edge stands.
The warning states that edges are missing from this answer; it never states that
the seed calls nothing more.

callees.description: Edges the walk dropped over every depth, one per call the engine named.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

oneOf.description:
The walk took a language engine's answer without progress evidence that the engine
had settled: it announced no work since it started or was last told of a changed
file, and stayed quiet past its `settle_delay`. The answer stands. An engine that
recomputes without announcing work may have answered before it read that change, and
a later read meets it settled.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

processes.description:
The engines the walk took unconfirmed, by accepted process key, sorted. Inline
processes use the exact language identity segment.

oneOf.description:
The history store the server fills in the background has not analyzed every commit
`[providers.history]` selects, so a commit search answers from the `analyzed` ones
alone and a commit the store has not reached answers nothing. The fill runs newest
first and continues without a request; a later search answers the rest.

analyzed.description: Commits the history store holds of the ones its latest fill selects.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

total.description: Commits the history store's latest fill selects.

oneOf.description:
The comparison reached `paths_max` changed paths and stopped there, so declarations
in the changed paths past it are missing from this answer. Narrow the comparison
with `paths`, or name two sides that differ in fewer files.

detail.description: Why the warning was raised - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

paths_max.description: Changed paths the comparison stopped at, equal to the bound it reached.

oneOf.description:
Global access is disabled under `[global] enabled = false`, so the answer carries no
package facts.
The global API could not answer, so the answer carries no package facts.

failure_class.description: Bounded class of the global API failure.

oneOf.description:
The global API advertised a publication the client cannot read, so the answer
carries no package facts.

failure_class.description: Bounded class of the incompatible publication.

oneOf.description:
The global API returned an invalid or truncated response, so the answer carries no
package facts.

failure_class.description: Bounded class of the invalid response.

oneOf.description:
The global package page carried a bounded condition while its items remained valid.
`warning_code` identifies the condition and `detail` carries its bounded explanation.
`capability_unavailable` also names a feature the global API's capabilities do not
advertise, such as `patterns` for a `pattern` search, and the answer then carries the
project hits alone.

detail.description:
Optional bounded explanation returned by the global package service, or the
feature its capabilities do not advertise.

warning_code.description:
Stable condition code returned by the global package service, or
`capability_unavailable` for a feature its capabilities do not advertise.

oneOf.description:
The global publication holds no release of an exact package the dependency
context names, so nothing answers for it. At most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package
and dependency-context warnings ride one answer.

package.description: The exact package absent from the global publication.

oneOf.description:
The global publication holds no release a declared requirement admits, so nothing
answers for it. At most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context
warnings ride one answer.

entry.description: The declared requirement absent from the global publication.

oneOf.description:
The global publication holds no release at the exact version the dependency context
names, or none inside the range a declared requirement states, so the collected
release nearest it answers in its place: the package facts for `entry` come from
`package`. At most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context warnings
ride one answer.

entry.description: The dependency context entry, as the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state it.

package.description: The collected release that answers for `entry`.

oneOf.description:
The dependency context names a package no public registry serves: a path outside
the workspace, a git repository, a private registry, or a URL. No global package
index answers for it, and `reason` names the capability Rift does not have yet. At
most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context warnings ride one
answer.

entry.description:
The dependency context entry, as the workspace's manifests and lockfiles state
it; its `availability` names the kind.

reason.description: Why no global package index answers for the entry, for a reader.

oneOf.description:
One resolver or standard library probe read less than the workspace states, or the
context passed the bound on the entries one read carries, the smaller of the
server's own and the one the global API advertises, and its entries sorted last left:
every held entry before any the request's `packages` names. The dependency context
may then miss packages or name a standard library by its static reading. Rides only an answer whose `scope`
reaches packages; at most `DEPENDENCY_WARNINGS_MAX` package and dependency-context
warnings ride one answer, this one first, in resolver order.

reason.description: What the resolver could not do - prose for a reader; nothing keys on it.

resolver.description:
What degraded: a resolver by its manager name, `cargo`, `uv`, `npm`, or `bun`, a
standard library entry, `stdlib/rust`, `stdlib/node`, or `stdlib/python`, or the
package manager whose held or requested entries left past the entry bound, such
as `pypi`.

RelationshipFacet.description:
One portable category an edge falls into. The local kinds `import` and `use` can share
the `imports` facet, which lets one query cross languages.

RevisionId.description:
Identity of one revision in the workspace's version-control history, spelled the way the
version-control system spells it: a branch, tag, or commit id, optionally followed by
ancestry suffixes, such as `HEAD~2` for the second first-parent ancestor or `main^2` for
the second parent. Rift carries it opaquely and never orders two revisions by comparing
their identifiers.

SourceExcerpt.description:
A copy of source from the catalog. The unit may belong to the project, a dependency, or
the standard library; the excerpt preserves bytes as they were when the answer was
produced.

span.description: The source unit and byte range the text was taken from.

text.description: The source bytes returned by the request.

SourcePosition.description: One exact position in a project, package or runtime source unit.

character.description: Zero-based offset counted using the request's position encoding.

unit.description: Canonical physical source unit, independent of the logical symbol owner.

SourceUnitSpan.description: One byte range in a source-catalog unit.

range.description: Half-open UTF-8 byte range in that unit.

SymbolAlternative.description: An actual object proposed after a valid exact miss.

id.description: The candidate's actual canonical identity, including its exact owner and version.

match_context.description: Structural comparisons that explain this candidate.

SymbolDeclaration.description: One source binding for a logical object. Source-less objects have no bindings.

documentation_indices.description: Entries in the result symbol's documentation array supplied by this declaration.

line.description: One-based line where this declaration begins.

node.description: Source node when available and requested.

origin.description: Contextual owner and source kind of this declaration's source.

path.description: Repository-relative path. Exactly one of `path` and `unit` is present.

range.description: The declaration's complete byte range in its source.

signature_indices.description: Entries in the result symbol's signature array supplied by this declaration.

source.description: Source excerpt when requested and available.

source_complete.description: Whether the supplied excerpt contains this declaration's complete source.

type_indices.description: Entries in the result symbol's type array supplied by this declaration.

unit.description: Released source unit. Exactly one of `path` and `unit` is present.

SymbolHistory.description:
One symbol's timeline across the workspace's version-control history, newest revision
first. The timeline follows first parents from the served revision, or the selected
releases in version order, through the revisions the history store holds, and follows
the declaration's file across a rename that kept its bytes. It is bounded by
`[providers.history] max_revisions` and by a shallow clone's boundary.

complete.description:
Whether the timeline reached the repository's first commit. `false` when the
`max_revisions` bound, a shallow clone's boundary, or the oldest selected release
ended it first, or while the history store has not yet analyzed the served
revision, so revisions older than the listed ones may have touched the symbol.

symbol.description: The symbol the timeline is for.

versions.description: Revisions that touched the symbol, newest first.

SymbolIdentity.description: Canonical logical symbol identity with local, registered local, package or runtime ownership. The portable codec validates exact versions, UTF-8 and canonical percent-encoding before lookup.

SymbolMatchContext.description: The structural parts compared when an alternative was selected.

detail.description: Unfinished candidate work, when the complete nearest set could not be proved.

id.description: The valid exact identity requested by the caller.

SymbolUnavailableReason.description: Why an exact selection cannot establish presence or definite absence.

SymbolVersion.description:
One revision that touched a symbol. The history provider parses the declaration at each
first-parent revision that changed its file and classifies adjacent states; a revision
whose source cannot be parsed contributes no version.

author.description: Who authored the revision, as the version control records it.

kind.description: How the revision changed the symbol.

path.description: Where the declaration lived at that revision.

revision.description: The revision that touched the symbol.

summary.description: The revision's own first summary line, where the version control records one.

timestamp.description:
When the revision was committed, as RFC 3339 date-time carrying the recorded offset:
the committer time, not the author time.

SymbolVersionKind.description: What the revision did to the symbol.
